record.original_question: If F is finitely generated over a prime field or over an algebraically closed field, must any two quaternion division algebras over F that have the same finite splitting fields, or even just the same maximal subfields, already be isomorphic?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.5. Show that if F is a field which is finitely generated over a prime field or over an algebraically closed field, then any two quaternion division algebras having the same finite splitting fields (or even just the same maximal subfields) must be isomorphic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field that is either finitely generated over its prime field or finitely generated over an algebraically closed field. A quaternion algebra over $F$ is a $4$-dimensional central simple $F$-algebra; it is a division algebra if it has no nonzero zero-divisors. A field extension $L/F$ is called a splitting field of a quaternion division $F$-algebra $D$ if $D \otimes_F L \cong M_2(L)$. A maximal subfield of $D$ is a subfield $K \subseteq D$ containing $F$ that is maximal among commutative subfields (equivalently, a quadratic extension of $F$ embedding into $D$).

Let $D_1$ and $D_2$ be two quaternion division algebras over $F$. Suppose that $D_1$ and $D_2$ have the same set of finite splitting fields (i.e., for every finite extension $L/F$, $L$ splits $D_1$ if and only if $L$ splits $D_2$); or, more strongly, suppose merely that $D_1$ and $D_2$ have the same set of (isomorphism classes of) maximal subfields.

Must $D_1$ and $D_2$ be isomorphic as $F$-algebras?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, posed by Prasad and Rapinchuk, remains open in general. Significant partial results are known: Garibaldi and Saltman proved an affirmative answer when $F$ is an extension of a global field $K$ such that $F/K$ is unirational with trivial unramified Brauer group, and Krashen–McKinnie and others have established related cases. Counterexamples exist for very large (non-finitely-generated) fields, but for the finitely generated setting in the problem the question is still considered open.

status_evidence.title: Quaternion Algebras with the Same Subfields (Garibaldi–Saltman)
status_evidence.snippet: Prasad and Rapinchuk asked if two quaternion division F-algebras that have the same subfields are necessarily isomorphic. The answer is known to be 'no' for some very large fields. We prove the answer is 'yes' if F is an extension of a global field K so that F/K is unirational with trivial unramified Brauer group.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is attributed to Prasad–Rapinchuk; partial affirmative results in special finitely generated cases; counterexamples only for very large fields.

status_evidence.title: Distinguishing division algebras by finite splitting fields
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when division algebras over a field F are determined up to isomorphism by their finite splitting fields.
status_evidence.claim: Related question on finite splitting fields is actively studied with partial results.

status_evidence.title: Division algebras with the same maximal subfields (Chernousov survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the Prasad–Rapinchuk question on division algebras determined by their maximal subfields.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem remains open and is an active area of research.
